bullets: Many people have not realised they are pregnant yet.
A tiny ball of cells is settling into the lining of the womb.
Hormone levels are rising, and a home test may start to show a result.
askProvider: Ask when to book your first appointment and who to contact with questions.

bullets: The first layers of your baby's body are forming.
A very early heart and the beginnings of the brain and spine are taking shape.
Tiredness and sore breasts are common for many people.
askProvider: Ask which supplements, medicines and foods are fine to keep taking or to avoid.

bullets: A heartbeat may be seen on an early scan around now.
Queasiness, a keen sense of smell and tiredness are common for many people.
Your baby is growing quickly, even though you may not look pregnant yet.
askProvider: Ask what to do if the queasiness makes it hard to eat or drink.

bullets: Tiny buds that will become arms and legs are appearing.
Your baby's face is starting to form.
Many people feel tired, queasy or emotional. This is very common.
askProvider: Ask what appointments and tests to expect over the next few weeks.

bullets: Fingers and toes are starting to form.
Your baby is already making small movements, far too small to feel.
Many people need more rest. Short naps can help.
askProvider: Ask which scans and checks are offered, and roughly when.

bullets: Your baby's major organs are developing.
Tiny ears and eyelids are forming.
Mood changes are common, and so is feeling worn out.
askProvider: Ask what you can do about symptoms that bother you, such as heartburn or headaches.

bullets: Your baby's vital organs are in place and carry on growing.
Little hands can bend at the wrists.
Many people notice their waist and clothes feeling different.
askProvider: Ask what to do if you have bleeding, strong pain or anything that worries you.

bullets: Your baby is moving about, still too small for you to feel.
Fingernails and tiny tooth buds are forming.
You may notice more energy soon, though everyone is different.
askProvider: Ask about the screening tests that are offered and what each one looks for.

bullets: Your baby's reflexes are developing.
Their kidneys are starting to work.
The first three months are almost over, and many people feel a little better.
askProvider: Ask when to expect your results and who will share them with you.

bullets: Your baby can curl their fingers and may suck a thumb.
Their body is catching up with their head in size.
Many people notice more energy as the second trimester begins.
askProvider: Ask whether there is anything to change in your work, exercise or travel plans.

bullets: Your baby can make small facial movements.
Fine hair, called lanugo, is starting to grow.
Appetite often returns, and queasiness often eases.
askProvider: Ask what a healthy amount of weight gain is for you.

bullets: Your baby's bones are getting harder.
Your baby may be able to sense light through closed eyelids.
You might notice a nosebleed or stuffy nose. Hormones can cause both.
askProvider: Ask which routine checks, such as blood pressure and urine tests, will happen at each visit.

bullets: Your baby's legs are growing longer than their arms.
Some people feel the first flutters now or in the next few weeks, a feeling often called quickening.
Back aches and round-ligament twinges are common as your womb grows.
askProvider: Ask when your detailed scan is, and what it checks.

bullets: Your baby is building a layer of fat under the skin.
Their skeleton is changing from soft cartilage to bone.
Your appetite may be bigger than before.
askProvider: Ask which exercises are comfortable and safe for you.

bullets: Your baby may yawn and hiccup. You cannot feel hiccups yet.
Their ears are in position and starting to pick up sounds.
Dizziness when standing up quickly is common. Rising slowly helps.
askProvider: Ask what to do if you feel dizzy, faint or very breathless.

bullets: A protective coating called vernix is covering your baby's skin.
Their senses of touch, taste, sight and hearing are developing.
Leg cramps are common at night for many people.
askProvider: Ask about your anatomy scan, and whether you can bring someone with you.

bullets: You are about halfway there.
From now, length is measured from head to heel, so the number jumps.
Many people feel movement more clearly each week.
askProvider: Ask how to tell your baby's usual pattern of movement as it develops.

bullets: Your baby moves a lot, and you may feel it as kicks, rolls or flutters.
They swallow small amounts of fluid and practise digesting.
Your skin, hair and nails may change a little.
askProvider: Ask which kinds of pain or tightening are normal at this stage.

bullets: Your baby's eyebrows and eyelids are fully formed.
They can hear your voice and other sounds, though muffled.
Swollen feet and ankles are common by the end of the day.
askProvider: Ask when swelling is something to mention straight away.

bullets: Your baby's skin is wrinkled and will fill out as they gain fat.
They respond to loud noises and may move when startled.
Some people have occasional practice tightenings of the womb.
askProvider: Ask how to tell practice tightenings from something you should report.

bullets: Your baby's lungs are developing the branches that will carry air.
Their sleep and wake times are becoming more regular.
Itchy skin and stretch marks are common.
askProvider: Ask whether you will be offered a test for gestational diabetes, and when.

bullets: Your baby's hands are developed enough to grasp.
Their hair is growing and may have colour.
Heartburn and trouble sleeping are common for many people.
askProvider: Ask what helps with sleep and heartburn in pregnancy.

bullets: Your baby's eyes begin to open.
They are practising breathing movements with amniotic fluid.
Your back may ache more as your bump grows.
askProvider: Ask about the vaccines offered in pregnancy and when.

bullets: Your baby is moving through regular cycles of sleep and activity.
Their brain is growing quickly.
Many people feel more tired again as the third trimester nears.
askProvider: Ask how you will be asked to keep track of your baby's movements.

bullets: The third trimester begins.
Your baby can blink and respond to light.
Your provider may ask you to keep track of your baby's movements. This app has a kick counter for that.
askProvider: Ask how many movements, over what time, your provider wants you to watch for, and who to call if they feel different.

bullets: Your baby's muscles and lungs keep maturing.
They have less room to move, so movements may feel different.
Heartburn, breathlessness and a sore back are common.
askProvider: Ask what a usual pattern of movement means for you and when to call.

bullets: Your baby's brain is making many new connections.
They are gaining weight steadily.
You may feel clumsy or get tired more easily. Rest when you can.
askProvider: Ask what to do if your waters break, and what to do if you have bleeding.

bullets: Your baby can turn their head from side to side.
Their senses are working well.
Many people need the toilet more often as the baby presses on the bladder.
askProvider: Ask which signs mean you should call, and which number to use day or night.

bullets: Your baby's toenails and fingernails are fully formed.
They practise breathing and may have hiccups you can feel.
Braxton Hicks practice tightenings may become more noticeable.
askProvider: Ask how to tell practice tightenings from the real thing.

bullets: Your baby's bones are hardening, except the skull, which stays soft for birth.
Their immune system is developing.
Sleep can be hard. Pillows between the knees help many people.
askProvider: Ask what your birth plan options are, and who to share your plan with.

bullets: Your baby's lungs and nervous system keep maturing.
Many babies settle into a head-down position around now or in the next weeks.
It can be a good time to start packing a hospital bag.
askProvider: Ask what pattern of contractions, such as 5-1-1, your provider wants you to watch for before calling, and the number to call.

bullets: Your baby is putting on weight quickly and has less room to move.
Their kidneys are working and their liver is developing.
You may feel pressure low in your pelvis and need to pass urine often.
askProvider: Ask when and where you should go if you think labor might be starting.

bullets: Your baby may be getting into position for birth.
Your appointments may now be more frequent.
Many people feel tired and impatient. This is normal.
askProvider: Ask what to bring, and whether your partner can come to appointments and the birth.

bullets: Many babies are born between now and 42 weeks.
Your baby can grasp firmly and practises sucking.
Practice tightenings may get stronger and more frequent.
askProvider: Ask what your provider wants you to do if your baby moves less than usual.

bullets: Your baby's organs are ready for life outside, and they keep growing.
They may drop lower into your pelvis.
Many people feel excited, nervous and ready for it to be over all at once.
askProvider: Ask who to call first when contractions start, and when to leave for the hospital or birth center.

bullets: Your baby's brain and lungs are still developing.
The practice tightenings may feel different from earlier ones.
Rest, eat well and keep your bag and phone numbers ready.
askProvider: Ask what happens if your baby has not arrived by your due date.

bullets: This is your estimated due date week. Only a few babies arrive on the day itself.
Your baby is about the size they will be at birth, give or take.
Your provider will talk with you about what to expect from here.
askProvider: Ask when you will be seen next and what the plan is if you go past your due date.

bullets: Many people go past their due date. It is common, especially with a first baby.
Your provider may offer extra checks and talk about next steps.
Keep resting, and keep tracking your baby's movements.
askProvider: Ask what extra checks are offered, and what the options are if labor does not start by itself.

bullets: Past your due date, your provider will guide next steps.
You may be seen more often, with extra checks.
Contact your provider any time you feel unsure or worried.
askProvider: Ask what the plan is for the next few days, and who to call at any hour.
